newsitem.title: UK: BoE's George - pound cut push RPIX down to target.
newsitem.headline: BoE's George - pound cut push RPIX down to target.

text.p: Bank of England Governor Eddie said on Monday that the Bank's forecasts were not an exact science and it was not impossible that the pound's strength could force inflation down to the government's target.

"This isn't totally precise. It is not inconceivable over the next few months that the strength of sterling comes through more rapidly into retail prices and that actually at the end of parliament...we could indeed be at 2.5 percent," George told parliament's Treasury Select Committee.
"In that case one would say, well policy wasn't too loose."
The government has a medium-term target of 2.5 percent for underlying inflation. The Bank's inflation report, released last week, called for a moderate rate rise if that target was to be met.
"The important thing is that we can never guarantee we know what can deliver 2.5 percent inflation or less. We say what we think is necessary," George said.
The Bank adjusts its projections in the light of what is going on all the time, George said.
